claim: For a MgO test set, M3GNet outperforms Moment Tensor Potentials in extrapolating equation-of-state behavior beyond the training regime and exhibits long-range interaction characteristics similar to a Buckingham + Coulomb model.

claim: M3GNet molecular-dynamics simulations of Li3YCl6 reproduce ionic conductivity (14.3 mS cm-1) and activation energy (0.22 eV) consistent with ab-initio MD, and short-time MD correctly identifies known lithium superionic conductors by their high mean-squared displacements at elevated temperatures.

claim: Screening 31.7 million hypothetical crystals with M3GNet identifies approximately 1.8 million candidates with predicted hull distances below 0.001 eV/atom, and among the 2,000 lowest-energy candidates, 1,578 are confirmed stable (Ehull < 0.001 eV/atom) by DFT.

claim: The final M3GNet interatomic potential achieves test mean absolute errors of 0.035 eV/atom for energy, 0.072 eV/Å for forces, and 0.41 GPa for stresses on a held-out Materials Project dataset covering 89 elements.

claim: Training M3GNet on energies alone (M3GNet-E) yields force and stress mean absolute errors larger than the intrinsic data dispersion, demonstrating that forces and stresses must be included in training.
held_out: claim: A single universal M3GNet model trained simultaneously on six elements attains error metrics comparable to element-specific M3GNet models.

claim: A single-CPU M3GNet relaxation completes in about 22 seconds, compared with 15 hours on 32 cores for DFT; pre-relaxation with M3GNet shortens subsequent DFT relaxation time by roughly a factor of three and reduces total CPU time by an average factor of 2.97.

claim: M3GNet predicts phonon band structures and densities of states for SiO2 polymorphs that quantitatively agree with DFT calculations, and the predicted phonon density-of-states center follows the expected ω ∝ 1/√m trend across materials.

claim: On the MD17 and MD17-CCSD(T) molecular force-field benchmarks, M3GNet achieves lower energy and force errors than the Embedded Atom Neural Network and comparable accuracy to state-of-the-art message-passing and equivariant neural networks; when benchmarked against quantum-accurate CCSD/CCSD(T) data, it attains state-of-the-art accuracy for several molecules.
claim: Relaxing test crystals with M3GNet reduces median volume error from 2.4 % to 0.6 % and energy mean absolute error from 0.169 eV/atom to 0.035 eV/atom relative to DFT-relaxed references.
claim: The M3GNet architecture preserves continuity of energies, forces, and stresses with respect to changes in bond count, satisfying a necessary physical constraint for interatomic potentials.
